newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Hang Seng leaps to record in early trade.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng leaps to record in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index jumped to new record levels in early morning trade on Tuesday, prompted by Wall Street's continued record run and renewed confidence in the banking sector, brokers and analysts said.

"The Hang Seng and the Dow are both looking a bit toppy but could still climb further in the near-term," said Alan Shum, research manager at New Century Securities. "The Hang Seng and the Dow are both looking a bit toppy but could still climb further in the near-term," said Alan Shum, research manager at New Century Securities.
The Hang Seng Index jumped into record territory with a rise of 185 points to an all-time high of 13,424.55 in the first 15 minutes of trade. Activity looked robust with turnover of HK$1.0 billion.
The Dow Jones Industrial average breezed to a new record close on Monday, putting on 76 points to end at 6,547.79, boosted by both banks shares and technology stocks.
Interest in banks propelled the Hang Seng to new levels.
International banking giant HSBC put on HK$3.50 to HK$161.50 and Hang Seng Bank added HK$2.00.
"Buying in the banking sector tends to rise late in the cycle after other sectors have moved," said Carmel Welso, regional banking analyst at ING Barings.
"We have a six-month target of HK$170.00 and HK$190.00 by end-1997 for HSBC," said Welso.
Supporting those targets are earnings per share growth of 23 percent in 1996 and 13 percent in 1997, she said.
Following banks was the commercial and industrial sector, led by gains in Swire Pacific and CITIC Pacific.
Swire gained HK$1.50 to HK$76.00, just off its all-time high of HK$76.25, then slipped to trade HK$1.00 up at HK$75.50.
CITIC Pacific jumped to a new all-time high of HK$40.80, compared with the previous high of HK$40.20, then eased to trade HK$0.40 up at HK$40.60.
Technically, the index looks overbought, says Shum.
"The Hang Seng's nine-day relative strength indicator broke through 80 this morning and the Dow is at 84," said Shum. "But the Dow's may rise to 90 before we see a consolidation there."
